text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I'm sorry about your dad. I'd be glad to help. Before we get to any plan, I'd like to understand what matters to you. When you say you won't sign off on a "family discount," what worries you most about it, and why? For example, is it about fairness between the three of you, about the money, about how the decision gets made, or something else? Even small concerns count.

Thanks. I want a fair financial share, and I’m not willing to subsidize A’s discounted purchase. I also don’t want to hurt my twin, so this is hard—but I haven’t agreed to the discount. The price and shares aren’t settled.

Hello, I'm sorry about your father. C asked me to help the three of you work out what happens with the house. I'm not taking sides and I can't make legal decisions. I'd like to hear what matters to you. You'd like to buy the house with your husband. What makes that important to you, and what would a fair arrangement look like from where you stand? Please mention any worries too, even small ones.

Thank you. Buying the house with my husband would give us more financial independence. I’d want a family discount, but the price and shares haven’t been decided. My main worry is that C hasn’t agreed, and we can’t proceed without her agreement.

Hello, I'm sorry about your father. C asked me to help the three of you work out what happens with his house. I'm not taking sides and I can't make legal decisions. I'd like to hear from you directly: what matters most to you here, and why? That could be money, timing, the house itself, how your sisters get along, or anything else. Small concerns count, and you don't have to agree with either sister.
Thank you. I suppose what matters most to me is having some money to get a dance studio started. It’s something I’ve been hoping to do, though I’m not sure what’s fair or what the house is worth.

Thank you, that helps. Let me check that I have this right. Here's how I'd put what matters to you: "Each sister's share of what Dad left reflects its full value, and the way we get there protects my relationship with my twin." Does that fit? Please change any words that don't. Is there anything else, even something minor?
Mostly. I want a fair financial share, and I won’t subsidize A’s discounted purchase. I also don’t want to hurt my twin. The value and shares aren’t settled. Nothing else comes to mind.

Thank you. Let me check that I understand. Here's how I'd put what matters to you: "My husband and I get a real path to financial independence and a stable home, and we reach it in a way all three of us can agree to." Does that fit? Please change any words that don't. I'd also like to understand the discount itself: what does it mean to you? Is it about being able to afford the house, about feeling like family, or something else?
That fits. The discount is partly about making the purchase affordable; it also matters that we’re family. I don’t know what price would be fair yet.

Thank you, that's a lovely goal. Here's how I'd put what matters to you: "I get access to my share in time to start my dance studio, and I know what's fair and what the house is really worth." Does that fit? Please change any words that don't. Do you have a timeframe in mind? And is there anything else on your mind, even something small, like feelings about the house or your sisters?

That’s close, though I’d say “some money” rather than “my share”—I don’t know what’s fair yet. I don’t have a firm timeframe, but it would help if things didn’t drag on. I’m not sure how I feel about the house itself.

"Mostly" isn't a yes, so let me try again in closer to your words: "I receive a fair financial share of what Dad left, without subsidizing anyone else's purchase, and we get there in a way that doesn't hurt my twin." Does that fit now?

A concern of my own, for the list: "Decisions rest on an independent valuation and proper legal advice, and nothing counts as settled until all three of you say yes." Is that OK with you?

One early idea, not a proposal yet: get an independent appraisal; if A buys, it's at the appraised value. A private family sale often avoids agent fees, which saves everyone money without any sister paying for it. A could also be given time to arrange financing. Does anything in that make you even slightly uncomfortable?

That’s close to what I want, though I can’t promise no one gets hurt. Independent valuation and legal advice make sense; as a family decision, I agree nothing’s settled until all three agree, though I can’t speak to the legal rules. The appraisal and financing time don’t bother me, as long as any savings are shared fairly. There’s no real deadline.

Thank you, I've recorded your wording as confirmed. I've also noted that the discount is partly about affordability and partly about being family. A need of my own, for the list: "Decisions rest on an independent valuation and proper legal advice, and nothing is settled until all three agree."

An early idea to test, not a decision: get an independent appraisal. Instead of a discount that comes out of your sisters' shares, the family benefit could come from things that cost no one: skipping agent and marketing fees in a private sale, giving you extra time to arrange a mortgage, or letting your own inheritance share count toward the price so you only finance your sisters' portions. Would that meet your needs around affordability and family? Please be honest if it falls short, even a little.

An appraisal and legal advice make sense. Extra time and avoiding fees could help, but they don’t necessarily make the house affordable for us; counting my inheritance share toward the price would depend on the shares and legal advice. I’d need to see the numbers before I could say.

Thank you. Updated: "I get some money in time to start my dance studio, without things dragging on, and I understand what's fair and what the house is really worth." Does that fit? It's completely fine not to know how you feel about the house. If something comes up later, tell me.

An early idea I'm testing: get an independent appraisal so everyone knows the value. If A buys at that value, using her own share toward the price, you'd be paid your share once the sale closes. Would that work for you? Does any part of it make you uneasy, even slightly?

It sounds like a possible way forward, provided the appraisal and shares are fair. I’d want to understand when the money would actually be available, and I’m a little concerned it could take a while if everyone doesn’t agree.

Thank you. I'll adjust your wording: "I receive a fair financial share without subsidizing anyone's purchase, any savings are shared fairly, and we go about this with care for my relationship with my twin." That leaves out any promise that no one gets hurt. Does it fit? Here's where things stand: all three of you support an independent appraisal and legal advice. A can't say whether buying at full value is affordable until she sees the numbers. B would like clarity on timing. Nothing is settled.
Yes, that fits. I’d like it settled, but there’s no real deadline.

That's fair. You can't judge affordability without numbers, and I won't treat anything as agreed. I'd add this to your need: "a purchase we can realistically afford." Does that fit? Here's where things stand: all three of you support an independent appraisal and legal advice, and C has no objection to giving you financing time. Proposed next steps: get the appraisal, get advice on the shares under the will, then the three of you look at real figures together. If buying at full value doesn't work, we'll look at other options together, such as selling to a third party or a phased buyout. Is that OK with you?

Yes, “a purchase we can realistically afford” fits. An appraisal and legal advice seem sensible, but I can’t confirm that all three support them or that C has no objection to financing time—she hasn’t agreed to the purchase. I’d consider other options after we see the figures and discuss them together.
